userStories.title: Telegram webhook + fast-ack pattern
userStories.description: As the operator, I want the bot to feel instant even though the work behind it is slow.
acceptanceCriteria: /api/telegram/webhook verifies Telegram's secret token header
Handler acknowledges every update (200 OK) in under 1s; slow work is dispatched async with results delivered via a follow-up sendMessage/editMessageText

Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: src/app/api/telegram/webhook/route.ts: verifies Telegram's X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header against TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, then delegates to a new src/lib/telegram-webhook.ts::handleTelegramWebhook, which is deliberately synchronous -- it schedules the real work via an injected scheduleAsync (the route passes Next 15's after()) and returns a {status, body} result immediately, never awaiting the deferred work. This is the fast-ack pattern: the route's NextResponse.json(...) goes out before any Claude/provider/DB call behind the update has even started, and after() keeps that work alive past the response without blocking it. Confirmed via direct experiment that Next's after() throws when called outside a real request scope ('after was called outside a request scope'), which is why handleTelegramWebhook takes scheduleAsync as a parameter rather than importing after() directly -- this is what makes the fast-ack property unit-testable at all. src/lib/telegram-webhook.ts::processTelegramUpdate is the deferred work itself: looks up the chat's bot_sessions row (src/actions/bot-sessions.ts: getPendingSession/setPendingSession/clearPendingSession, upserting on the table's unique chat_id), and if pendingEntityType is 'idea' with a pendingField of 'prompt' or 'caption', applies the incoming plain-text message via the existing shared action layer (editIdeaPrompt/editIdeaCaption from US-005's src/actions/ideas.ts, channel='telegram'), clears the session, and confirms via a new src/lib/telegram-client.ts (sendMessage/editMessageText against the real Bot API, wrapped in callWithRetry the same way the video-provider adapters are). The inline-keyboard buttons that create these pending sessions in the first place (Edit Prompt / Edit Caption / Change Provider) are US-014's job; this story only needed the generic session-routing engine to exist and be provably correct, which is what the multi-chat routing test below checks. bot_sessions table already existed in the schema from the Phase 0 groundwork -- no migration needed for this story. New tests: src/lib/telegram-webhook.test.ts (8 tests: auth rejection with no work scheduled, the fast-ack timing test using a controllable never-resolving promise for the 'slow operation' to prove the handler's result is produced before that promise is even invoked, and 5 processTelegramUpdate tests including one that seeds two different chats with two different pending sessions and confirms only the replying chat's idea/session is touched), src/lib/telegram-client.test.ts (4 tests for sendMessage/editMessageText request shape, Telegram-level ok:false handling, and retry-exhaustion), src/actions/bot-sessions.test.ts (5 tests for get/set/clear and upsert-not-duplicate behavior). Added seedBotSession to src/actions/test-helpers.ts. Per updated verification policy (agreed with the operator this session): tsc --noEmit clean, eslint . clean, vitest run 108/108 passing -- no manual Postgres/build/curl E2E for this story; that full cycle is now reserved for phase boundaries rather than every story, to keep pace reasonable.

New telegram-idea-card.ts renders an idea's card text and its Approve/Reject/Edit Prompt/Edit Caption/Change Provider keyboard (callback_data format 'idea:<action>:<id>'), plus notifyPendingIdeas(db, ideas) which pushes each freshly-generated idea to TELEGRAM_OPERATOR_CHAT_ID (no-op if Telegram env vars aren't set; per-idea failures are swallowed so a Telegram outage never breaks idea generation) -- wired into niches/actions.ts's generateIdeasAction right after generateIdeas. telegram-webhook.ts's processTelegramUpdate now branches on message vs callback_query: Approve/Reject call the exact same approveIdea/rejectIdea from US-005's shared action layer and then editMessageText the original card to show the final state with the keyboard removed (errors, e.g. double-tapping Approve on an already-decided idea, are caught and reported back via sendMessage rather than crashing the deferred after() work). Edit Prompt/Edit Caption set a bot_sessions pending row (pendingAction='awaiting_text') that US-013's plain-text handler already knew how to resolve. Change Provider is a two-step flow: since a provider id + an idea id together don't fit Telegram's 64-byte callback_data limit, tapping it sets a pending session (pendingAction='choosing_provider', entityId=ideaId) and sends a keyboard of enabled providers labeled with their live price (via estimateCost); picking one only needs to carry the provider id in callback_data, since the idea id is resolved from that same pending session, mirroring the existing session-based design from US-013 but driven by a button tap instead of a text reply. Per the operator-agreed lightened verification policy: tsc --noEmit clean, eslint . clean, vitest run 124/124 passing (16 new tests) -- no manual Postgres/build/curl E2E for this story; a full E2E pass is planned once US-015 (video approval via Telegram) also lands, closing out Phase 4.
